title: introduce-stream-sanitizer-window-and-functioncall-flush-to-preserve-json-span-contiguity
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Intermittent production incidents and fuzz tests revealed cases where SSE chunk boundaries could split JSON object spans or function-call sentinel tokens in ways that make downstream parsers emit truncated or mis-ordered events. This caused structured-output consumers and OpenAI-compatibility wrappers to drop function-call arguments or mis-associate tokens when partial frames were replayed. This PR introduces a lightweight streaming sanitizer layer and a small reflow window that: 1) keeps a minimal lookback buffer for boundary repair, 2) normalizes delimiter emission order for function/tool-call sentinels, and 3) applies a safe escape-rewrite for split UTF-8/JSON token fragments. The description below summarizes changes, risks, testing, and rollout plan. Changes made: - runtime/sse/stream_window.go: new StreamSanitizer that maintains a sliding reflow window (configurable max bytes, default 4KB) and detects partial JSON spans using a fast heuristic (brace/quote counters + UTF-8 continuation checks). When a span crosses the window boundary the sanitizer defers emit and attempts repair by joining adjacent chunks or emitting a rescue-marker event. - runtime/sse/protocol.go: added deterministic ordering guarantees for sentinel emissions (heartbeat -> preamble -> function_call_start -> payload chunks -> function_call_end). This avoids reordered sentinel interleaving under high-concurrency flush. - openai/compat/adapter.py: adapter updated to understand the new rescue-marker event and to tolerate delayed function_call_end tokens; compatibility shim will buffer until a matching end or rescue marker. - runtime/kv/cache_adapter.rs: minor change to avoid flushing cached prefixes in the middle of an active function call stream. - tests/integration/sse_partial_json_test.go: new deterministic and randomized tests that simulate chunk-split UTF-8 and nested JSON objects across many micro-batches. - docs/compat/notes_sse_chunking.md: notes for integrators about rescue-marker semantics and upgraded adapter behavior. Implementation notes: - The sanitizer is intentionally conservative: by default it only defers emission for spans <4KB and recent activity; longer objects are passed through to avoid unbounded buffering. - UTF-8 sequences and escape sequences are validated with a fast-path routine; malformed runs trigger a rescue-marker plus the raw bytes (so higher-level telemetry can decide). - The functioncall sentinel ordering change is idempotent for well-formed streams; adapters that already respect function_call_start/end are unchanged. Rollout and migration: - Feature gated behind runtime flag "sse.stream_sanitizer.enabled" (default: off in canary). - Canary rollout to 5% of hosts for 48 hours; telemetry checks for increased latency, increased memory use, and rescued-frame rate. - If rescue rate >0.1% or p95 latency regression >10% we will roll back the gate. Testing and validation: - CI: added unit tests for boundary heuristics and integration test harness that replays recorded truncated-chunk incidents. - Staging: ran long-run fuzz and compatibility suite against openai-compat adapter; observed 0 parity regressions and eliminated a previously reproducible tool-call-argument-drop case. - Load test: negligible CPU increase on average, tail latencies increased by ~3ms in worst-case (within SLO). Review summary and discussion: - Jordan: "Core heuristic looks reasonable; ensure the window size is configurable per-customer since some private deployments may accept higher buffering." Ava: "Added config path and documented VPC override in installer notes." - Maya: "What about cascade effects with autoscaler when many hosts buffer?" Ava: "Sanitizer uses soft memory caps per-worker and will spill to disk after soft cap; we added a metric sse.sanitizer.spill_count and autoscaler alerts to the rollouts." - Ethan: "Adapter changes look safe but add a migration note for older clients." Ava: "Added compatibility shim to adapter.py that keeps old behavior if client declares legacy-mode." CI and merge: - CI initially caught a flaky test in the randomized harness; fixed by tightening the timing window and re-running. - All checks passed on the final run (unit, integration, lint, format, OSS compatibility). - Merge method: squash and merge. Related: ENG-4523 (streaming reliability), SUP-1290 (customer incident report). Release notes: "Fixes where SSE chunking could split JSON or function-call sentinels, causing truncated structured output for some OpenAI-compat consumers. Introduces a stream sanitizer and rescue-marker semantics; disabled by default during canary rollout." Risks and mitigations: "Increased memory under pathological inputs (mitigated via soft cap and spill-to-disk), and potential small p95 latency increase (observed <=3ms in load tests). Rollback plan included. Follow-ups: add server-side telemetry to track rescued-span types and a developer CLI to reassemble rescued frames for debugging.

release_notes: Fixes to SSE chunking that preserve JSON/tool-call boundaries by adding a stream sanitizer and rescue markers; canary-gated rollout.
notes_for_oncall: If a canary report shows rescue_rate spike or p95 regression, disable sse.stream_sanitizer.enabled via flags service. Metric names: sse.sanitizer.rescue_rate, sse.sanitizer.spill_count, sse.sanitizer.window_size_bytes.
